newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front page - May 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front page - May 12.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on Monday:
WASHINGTON - Employment discrimination cases are surging into federal courts in record numbers, more than doubling in the past four years because of new laws and new attitudes in the workplace.
NEW YORK - The IBM supercomputer Deep Blue decisively beat world chess champion Garry Kasparov, the first time a computer has been able to defeat the best human player in a match.

WASHINGTON - Most District of Columbia residents say the D.C. financial control board has not done a good job improving the quality of public schools and other city services in the two years since its creation by Congress, a new poll shows.

MOSCOW - The breakdown of law enforcement and the proliferation of private armies and protection rackets prone to ruthless gangland tactics are threatening Russia's young democracy and free-market economy.
WASHINGTON - Erskine Bowles, a banker who become President Bill Clinton's Chief of Staff, has stressed process rather than ideology in his White House job.

LILLIAN, ALABAMA - A team of 10-year-old baseball players in Alabama has been disbanded after a series of controversies unleashed when some players refused to wear jerseys sporting the name of the team's sponsor, a video store that also rents some 500 X-rated films.
